types.description: A value computed by a database function the project owns (rc.21): @function names it, @schema its schema (absent: public), and @args the fields passed to it, in order. On an entity an argument is one of its fields; on a projection, one of its own fields (not an aggregate) or a field of its base entity. @params declares each argument's type and @returns the result's: an argument must have its parameter's type (cast it through an origin.computed field otherwise), @returns must be the carrying field's subtype, and the view casts the call to the field's full column type (the one its table column would have: length or @dbColumnType spelling, precision and scale, a local or zoned timestamp), so the call is checked, never free SQL. The signature is a declaration: meta verify --db reads the function from pg_proc and fails on a parameter or return type that differs. MetaObjects never creates the function: it is owned SQL, created before the view. Declared on an entity, it is entity-derived: a projection reaching the entity reads it like any derived field. Postgres only; the SQLite view emitter refuses it.
types.whenToUse: A view column is the result of a function the database already holds (a PL/pgSQL state machine, a legacy computation) and cannot be expressed in @expr. Declare the call instead of hand-writing the view's @sql.

children.name: function
children.description: The function's name as the database names it: a plain identifier ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*), quoted when it is not lowercase.

children.name: schema
children.description: The schema the function lives in, a plain identifier. Absent: public.

children.name: args
children.description: The fields passed to the function, in parameter order: field names of the host entity, or (on a projection) of the projection or its base entity. Each must be a scalar field whose subtype is the declared parameter type in @params; to pass another type, pass an origin.computed field that casts it ({ cast: { field: x }, as: <param> }). Absent or empty: a function of no arguments.

children.name: params
children.description: The function's declared parameter types, one field subtype per @args entry, in order (string, int, long, double, float, decimal, boolean, date, timestamp, uuid). Required when @args is not empty; an argument of another type is refused (ERR_INVALID_ORIGIN).

children.name: returns
children.description: The function's declared return type, a field subtype; it must be the carrying field's subtype (ERR_INVALID_ORIGIN). The view casts the call to the field's full column type, which would hide a wrong declaration, so meta verify --db checks it against the function's real return type (pg_proc).

children.name: union
children.description: rc.21: the view is this projection's rows UNIONed with each named projection's rows. Each named projection has the same effective fields as this one, in order: names, subtypes, array-ness and physical column names (ERR_BAD_ATTR_VALUE otherwise); its own @filter, joins and base apply to its rows. Usually this projection extends one branch and names the others. A named projection may be abstract and sourceless.

children.name: unionAll
children.description: rc.21: with @union, keep duplicate rows (UNION ALL). Absent or false: duplicates are removed (UNION), SQL's own default.

children.name: grain
children.description: rc.21: the view has one row per element of this base-entity field, a field.object array stored as jsonb; a base row with no element has no row. A field whose origin.passthrough @from names the field's @objectRef value object (Address.city) reads that member of the element; the base's own fields read the parent row as usual. An origin.aggregate is refused on such a projection.

children.name: grainOrdinal
children.description: rc.21: with @grain, the name of a field.int or field.long of this projection (with no origin) that holds the element's 1-based position in the array.
